source.note: Plan row 203 (Quaternius static Scythe via poly.pizza) is blocked, so this is Scythe.fbx from Quaternius's own CC0 Medieval Weapons Pack on OpenGameArt (same author, licence on the page; the same zip and pin as the sword and axe entries, and their colours, so the weapons read as one set). Height 1.7 m is the whole scythe, the bottom of the hooked snath to the top of its knob (a reaper's / war scythe, about head height on an adult). Rest pose: upright, snath along +Y with a gentle S-curve and a hooked foot on y = 0; blade flat in the XY plane (about 2 cm thick along Z), mounted by a collar at y 1.40 to 1.60 m, curving out toward +X and down to its tip at (+0.46, 1.33) m, with the concave cutting edge facing down toward the user and a short back spike to -X. The pipeline centres the bounding box, so the snath is not on the origin: its axis runs at z = 0 and x = -0.37 m near the foot, -0.28 m at mid grip and about -0.33 m along the bare upper shaft (y 0.85 to 1.40 m). The cord-wrapped grip runs from y 0.10 to 0.80 m. Two-handed hold: lower hand at about (-0.37, 0.25, 0) m, upper hand at about (-0.28, 0.70, 0) m; a one-handed carry (reaper pose) takes the upper hand point. To put it in a hand: parent to the hand, offset by minus that hand point in the scythe's frame (e.g. (+0.28, -0.70, 0) m for the upper hand), then rotate so Y runs along the fist's thumb direction and +X (the blade) points forward over the shoulder or out to the side. Colours match the sword: blade and back spike pale steel (moon over sky), snath, grip wrap and collar amber over sky.
